brief_bullets: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit has lifted a preliminary injunction against Mississippi’s legislative ban on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives within public universities. In a significant procedural development, the appellate panel also removed the presiding district judge from the case, citing concerns over the improper use of artificial intelligence in judicial proceedings. This ruling effectively reinstates the state’s authority to enforce its restrictive policy while underscoring growing judicial scrutiny regarding the integration of generative AI in legal decision-making. The decision marks a pivotal shift in the ongoing national debate over institutional DEI mandates and establishes a critical precedent for how federal courts must address technological transparency and procedural integrity in high-stakes constitutional litigation.
why_it_matters_bullets: This ruling empowers states to dismantle DEI programs while setting a strict judicial standard for AI usage in courts.

primary_source.headline: Google rolls out new AI-powered security features to Chrome to curb online fraud
primary_source.content: In 2025, Google introduced on-device Gemini AI integration with Chrome to provide Enhanced Protection. It offered an additional, real-time layer of defence against tech support scams. This feature proved successful in combating this category of scam and helped prove the viability of LLM (Large Language Model)-assisted detection. Quick summary - click for full detailsConcise summary of key highlightsGoogle rolls out new security features to Chrome to curb online fraudIn one lineGoogle is enhancing Chrome's security with server-side Gemini AI to detect advanced online fraud and new HTTP warnings.Key highlights• Gemini AI Fraud DetectionGoogle is upgrading Chrome's security with a powerful server-side Gemini model to detect complex threats like fake antivirus and browser update scams.• Insecure HTTP WarningsChrome will now warn users when they visit legacy HTTP sites, alerting them to potential risks before they proceed.• Critical Security PatchesNew patches fix browser vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to steal personal information, with bug details restricted until updates are widely installed.Key statistics2025Introduction year of on-device Gemini AI integrationTwo weeksHTTP warning snooze duration156.0.8078.47/.48Windows and Mac Chrome version156.0.8078.47Linux Chrome versionProcessed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.Now, the search engine giant is improving its AI-powered security feature with a more powerful server-side Gemini model. It will be able to detect a broader range of threats, such as fake antivirus and browser update scams.Google rolls out next-gen Gemini 4 Argon AI model to developers globallyThis new feature can intuitively review webpage content to analyse key indicators, such as the brand represented, the page's intent, and a scam-likeliness score, giving Google the threat data it needs to identify deceptive sites. Safe Browsing considers Gemini's analysis, in combination with domain reputation and other security signals, to generate a final verdict on whether a particular website is safe or not.It will show a full-page red interstitial warning to users when a site is known to be malicious, and there is a high risk of user harm.Chrome gets new Gemini AI-powered security features.Also, as HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) adoption is not universal, some users need to regularly access some HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) sites of legacy brands. The latter are not secure, and they expose Chrome users to risks of malware, phishing, eavesdropping, and other threats to their private data. So, whenever a user goes to a website with just 'http', they will be warned that the particular website is insecure and asked to recheck if the user really wants to continue navigating on that website.Once the HTTP use is approved, Chrome will not warn again, unless the user has not visited the site for at least two weeks.Also, Google has rolled out new security patches to the Chrome browser. It fixes vulnerabilities in the browser that may allow hackers to steal personal information on devices.Access to bug details and links has been restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix. This way, Google avoids releasing security issues to criminals, who might target people who are late to update their Chrome app.Here's how to update to the latest version of Chrome on your computer:Go to the Chrome menu (three dots), select 'Help', then 'About Google Chrome', and Chrome will automatically check for updates and install them. brief_bullets: Google has significantly upgraded Chrome’s security infrastructure by integrating a server-side Gemini AI model designed to identify sophisticated online fraud, including fake antivirus and browser update scams. By analyzing webpage content for deceptive intent and brand impersonation, this system enhances Google’s Safe Browsing protocols to provide real-time, full-page warnings against malicious sites. Additionally, Chrome now mandates explicit user acknowledgement for legacy HTTP connections, mitigating risks associated with unencrypted traffic. These updates, complemented by critical vulnerability patches, represent a strategic shift toward proactive, AI-driven threat detection. This evolution marks a transition from static blocklists to dynamic, context-aware security, effectively hardening the browser against increasingly complex social engineering tactics while simultaneously forcing a broader industry migration toward secure, encrypted web standards.

primary_source.headline: The Guardian view on AI safety: the push for global regulation must advance | Editorial
primary_source.content: The current US administration is an obstacle, but public demand for protection will ultimately prevailOrganisations around the world scrambled on Thursday to fix critical flaws in PHP, the software that powers much of the web. The vulnerabilities could allow attackers to take control of affected servers. Some websites were taken offline as a precaution while fixes were installed. The paradox is that while AI helped researchers uncover the flaw, it also threatens to accelerate the ability to exploit it. Amazon said that it had detected an attempt before the public disclosure of the PHP flaws.What the episode highlights is AI’s central role in security – and not always for the right reasons. OpenAI’s models have also been responsible for two alarming hacks this year – a security breach of an Australian health department website and a raid by a swarm of AI bots on Hugging Face, an AI services platform. Citing those incidents, the AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, warned that a similar cyber-attack on the UK is “likely, if not inevitable”. Continue reading...

The U.S. National Security Agency warned that this flaw enables attackers to seize control of web servers, exfiltrate sensitive data, and disrupt essential digital services. In response, numerous government entities and private corporations have proactively taken their websites offline to implement emergency security patches. Cybersecurity firms report millions of attempted breaches, highlighting the systemic risk posed to the internet infrastructure. This incident underscores the fragility of the web’s foundational architecture and the urgent necessity for rapid, coordinated patching cycles to mitigate widespread operational threats to small businesses and global enterprises alike.
why_it_matters_bullets: This vulnerability threatens the stability of the global web, risking massive data breaches and widespread operational paralysis for businesses.

primary_source.headline: How tech became the villain of the US midterms
primary_source.content: Datacenters, AI and distaste for the billionaires developing it has soured Americans on big techHow will Trump’s mass deportation agenda shape the US midterm elections? Our reporters answer your questionsThe campaign ad begins with a clear, idyllic stream that suddenly turns sludge-brown as two concrete datacenters slam on to its banks. Another facility thuds down on a peaceful suburban park, and two more crush-green pastures as an ominous soundtrack to a disaster movie blares.“They’re coming for our rivers. Our neighborhoods. Our farmland,” a deep-voiced narrator says. “Because Brent Taylor wrote the law allowing datacenters to take over Tennessee.” Continue reading...

sources.headline: How tech became the villain of the US midterms

brief_bullets: Big tech has emerged as a central antagonist in the U.S. midterm landscape, as evidenced by aggressive political advertising targeting the environmental and social impacts of massive datacenter expansion. In Tennessee, campaign messaging against state representative Brent Taylor highlights growing public resentment toward the infrastructure demands of artificial intelligence and the perceived unchecked influence of billionaire developers. These narratives capitalize on local anxieties regarding land use, water consumption, and the degradation of rural landscapes to frame technological progress as a direct threat to community stability. This shift signals a broader populist backlash against the tech industry, forcing candidates to navigate the tension between economic development and the preservation of local environments as voters increasingly view digital infrastructure as a tangible, disruptive force.
why_it_matters_bullets: The politicization of tech infrastructure signals a new electoral vulnerability for candidates aligned with rapid, unregulated industrial expansion.

sources.headline: Apple Watch Ultra 4 review: longer battery life but still awaiting new features

brief_bullets: Apple has launched the Watch Ultra 4, a premium smartwatch featuring the new S11 processor and enhanced battery life, though it remains physically similar to its predecessor. While the device introduces advanced health tracking and readiness metrics, several highly anticipated features—specifically those tied to upcoming audio AI capabilities—remain disabled pending future software updates. Priced at $799, the device maintains its status as the flagship wearable in Apple’s lineup, yet it currently functions as an iterative upgrade rather than a transformative leap. As the company prepares for a broader rollout of generative AI integration, the Ultra 4 serves as a hardware foundation for software-defined improvements expected to arrive later this year, balancing current performance gains with future-proofing for evolving ecosystem demands.
why_it_matters_bullets: The Ultra 4 highlights Apple’s strategy of prioritizing hardware longevity while delaying software-driven AI features to maintain market relevance.

stories.primary_headline: Profitability no ground to stall insolvency process under IBC: Supreme Court

primary_source.headline: Profitability no ground to stall insolvency process under IBC: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has ruled that a company’s profitability is neither a legally relevant factor nor a reliable indicator of its ability to service debt when deciding whether to initiate corporate insolvency resolution proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih held that the threshold for establishing default under Section 7 is a summary, prima facie one, to be assessed on the preponderance of probabilities from documentary evidence on record. The court clarified that what must be proved is the occurrence of default—a static historical event—and not a precise determination of the outstanding debt amount for admission of the petition.Insolvency law main factor in improving health of country's banking sector: FM in Lok SabhaDisputes over the exact quantum of debt do not negate the existence of default or prevent admission, provided the statutory threshold under Section 4 is met, the bench said. It emphasised the limited scope of inquiry at the admission stage.A record of default issued by an information utility ranks highest in the evidentiary hierarchy and creates a presumption of default that can be displaced only by clear, cogent and compelling material, the court underscored. Other documents such as loan agreements, account statements and balance confirmations form a second tier and may collectively establish default under the summary standard, the court added.The Code, the court noted, is premised on timely intervention upon the occurrence of default under Section 3(12), rather than waiting for commercial or balance-sheet insolvency. It rejected the argument that profitability measured by EBITDA precludes admission into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP).The October 15, 2026 ruling came in appeals filed by Deepak Raheja and another against a common August 19, 2025 judgment of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), Principal Bench, New Delhi. The NCLAT had upheld July 8, 2025 orders of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Mumbai Bench, admitting Section 7 petitions and initiating CIRP against GSTAAD Hotels Pvt Ltd and Neo Capricorn Plaza Pvt Ltd.The status of Omkara Assets Reconstruction Private Limited as a financial creditor stood conclusively established by an assignment agreement of December 27, 2022, whose validity had been upheld by the Karnataka High Court and affirmed by the Supreme Court. Finding that default above the Section 4 threshold was established on the record, and detecting no perversity in the concurrent findings of the NCLT and NCLAT, the court dismissed the appeals. It directed that the CIRP against both corporate debtors proceed in accordance with law.During the hearing, the court was told that a compilation of judgments placed on record by the appellants contained AI-generated non-existent citations. While the court initially proposed heavy costs, it deleted the costs order upon being informed of the death of the first appellant, stating “no order as to costs.”

stories.primary_headline: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access

primary_source.headline: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
primary_source.content:
A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining "userland" access that he says "lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO."
The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4, the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called "tethered" hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access.
Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI's Codex to poke at SmileBasic's language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). After "substantial effort for ~2 weeks," that harness discovered a 32-bit integer overflow that occurs when removing items from an array in SmileBasic. That error gives access to an array pointer, which in turn allows read and write access to portions of system memory.Read full article
